pois.name: Bow section
pois.note: Game scan marker at a commonly reported wreck-section position. The source grid gives the local seabed depth, while WHOI describes about 600 m between the sections. Marker geometry and placement do not constitute a georeferenced wreck survey.

pois.name: Stern section
pois.note: Game scan marker at a commonly reported wreck-section position. The source grid gives the local seabed depth, while WHOI describes about 600 m between the sections. Marker geometry and placement do not constitute a georeferenced wreck survey.

pois.name: Boiler field
pois.note: Local boiler-field scan marker near the stern. WHOI documents a boiler as the first recognised object in 1985; NOAA maps boilers in the 2010 debris survey. These accounts do not establish this exact marker coordinate or a surveyed boiler count here.

pois.name: Debris field (mid-site)
pois.note: Representative scan point between the hull sections. WHOI reports a 15–20 square mile survey area in 2010, distinct from individual debris clusters. No exact footprint for this marker is inferred.

pois.name: Where the "Big Piece" lay
pois.note: Approximate marker in the stern-side debris area. RMS Titanic Inc. reports recovery of the hull section in 1998; it is no longer on the seabed. This coordinate does not establish its historical resting place.

pois.name: Memorial plaque site (stern)
pois.note: Approximate stern memorial marker. The Titanic Historical Society confirms the 1986 placement on the stern; the exact aft-starboard footprint and a 1996 disappearance date were not verified against a primary source. No plaque is modelled.

pois.name: Unnamed seabed channel
pois.note: Eastern flank of a shallow NNE–SSW channel visible in the GMRT tile, ~4.8 km north-west of the bow (seabed 3,873 m here, axis ~3,890 m). This is survey data, not a reconstruction.
